verdicts_or_reports.expected: The subtask badge counts the full list of nested tasks (Pack for trip has 2 subtasks), so it stays "2" whether or not completed subtasks are shown.
verdicts_or_reports.observed: With "Show completed subtasks" ON and one subtask (Charge phone) completed, the badge reads 2. After turning "Show completed subtasks" OFF and completing Charge phone, the badge drops to 1. The badge count depends on the completed-subtask visibility filter instead of the full nested list.
steps: Start with Pack for trip expanded, subtasks Charge phone and Print tickets, badge shows 2.
Open Sort sheet, turn OFF 'Show completed subtasks', close the sheet.
Tap the checkbox of Charge phone to complete it.
Observe the Pack for trip badge: it reads 1 (expected 2).
Turn 'Show completed subtasks' back ON: badge reads 2 again with the same completed subtask, so the value follows the filter.

harness_replies: Developer: could not reproduce with the steps given.

sign_off.notes: Sweep of sorting/grouping, subtasks, and task search on Tasks.org. Checked: sort direction toggles (sorting and grouping) update the sheet and list order and persist across HOME/relaunch; grouping by due date (Thu/Tue/Fri/No due date) and by start date ("No start date") render correctly; descending order reverses the list; subtask expand/collapse, completing a subtask with Undo, and the subtask badge with completed subtasks shown (2 of 2 with one completed); search matches title and notes, subtask matches, ranking follows the active sort (ascending and descending gave reversed orders), no-match shows empty state, and opening a result opens the right task. Restored the sort/grouping settings and task states to the starting data. One observation filed: the Pack for trip badge drops from 2 to 1 when 'Show completed subtasks' is off and one subtask is completed; the developer could not reproduce it, so it is unresolved and my confidence is moderate. Not tested: start-date grouping with real Today/Tomorrow/overdue start dates (would require editing task data), deeper subtask nesting (no nested data present), and landscape layout beyond a single rotation check. Also note the rotation to landscape showed the list in a narrow pane, which I did not file.
